matches.quote: φ₁₂ is not reported for the 0° SQUID, where no chiral order is expected, under the same in-plane sweep protocol.
The data are taken at 20 K, whereas all other characterisation is at 60–74 K.
This history dependence is equally consistent with vortex trapping or depinning in the flakes or electrodes.
The slope relation δIs₁/δΦ = 1/(L_J,1 + Lgeo,1) holds only on specific branches, with sinusoidal-CPR assumptions.
The manuscript needs to reconcile how φ₁₂ ≈ π (rather than some intermediate 2φ₀) arises with a first-harmonic-dominated CPR.
It is also not shown how such a simulation compares with alternative states that also arise in a β ≈ 1 SQUID with a second harmonic.
Other needed checks: sweep-direction dependence; heating or retrapping effects in the counter-based protocol, where I⁺ and I⁻ are measured alternately; reproducibility after thermal cycling above Tc.
The inhomogeneity scenario is also an alternative explanation for TRSB, which the paper claims to rule out but does not test.
The "half-integer" points range roughly from 0.7π to 0.95π, and the "integer" points from 0.1π to 0.2π.
The comparison of the "superfluid stiffness" 1/L_J (an interlayer Josephson quantity ∝ Ic(T)) with bulk in-plane λ_ab⁻²(T) ∝ T² behaviour (Osborn thesis) is not like-for-like.

notes: C2 is partly matched by P9 (which critiques the validity of the analytical slope relation for L_J,1 without specifically citing the >20:1 vs 3:1 Ic ratio criterion). C4 is partly matched by P19 (which critiques the invalid comparison of 1/L_J(T) to bulk in-plane T^2 stiffness and asks for a proper Josephson baseline, rather than measuring L_J(T) on the 0-degree device). C10 is partly matched by P6/P18 (noting the unexplained choice of 20 K vs 60-74 K, without explicitly requesting a temperature sweep of the phase shift). C12 is partly matched by P2/P13 (attributing the few-percent diode asymmetry to field offsets or switching-protocol heating/retrapping artifacts rather than critical-current fluctuations). C13 is partly matched by P11/P21 (questioning why the observed shift uniquely implies opposite chirality versus second-harmonic metastable branches or fluxoid winding states, without mentioning faceting).
